def blocks(g,c):
    seen=set(); res=[]
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    for i in range(H):
        for j in range(W):
            if g[i][j]==c and (i,j) not in seen:
                st=[(i,j)]; comp=[]
                while st:
                    y,x=st.pop()
                    if (y,x) in seen or g[y][x]!=c: continue
                    seen.add((y,x)); comp.append((y,x))
                    for dy in(-1,0,1):
                        for dx in(-1,0,1):
                            st.append((y+dy,x+dx))
                rs=[p[0] for p in comp]; cs=[p[1] for p in comp]
                h=max(rs)-min(rs)+1; w=max(cs)-min(cs)+1
                res.append((h,w,min(rs),min(cs),len(comp)))
    return res

# Collect features for every bg cell across demos: d1,d2, n blocks at d1, n at d2, n at d1<=thr, n at d2<=thr, and label 3/1.
def feats(gi,go):
    H,W=len(gi),len(gi[0]); bl,bgc=blk_of(gi); out=[]
    for a in range(H):
        for b in range(W):
            if gi[a][b]!=bgc: continue
            ds=[(max(max(r0-a,a-(r0+h)),max(c0-b,b-(c0+w))),i) for i,(r0,c0,h,w) in enumerate(bl)]
            ds.sort(key=lambda x:x[0])
            f=dict(d1=ds[0][0],d2=ds[1][0],nd1=sum(v==ds[0][0] for v,_ in ds),nd2=sum(v==ds[1][0] for v,_ in ds),
                   n1d2=sum(v<=2 for v,_ in ds),n2d2=sum(v<=2 for v,_ in ds),
                   nd1_3=sum(v<=3 for v,_ in ds),label=go[a][b])
            out.append(f)
    return out
rows=[]
for k in range(1,6):
    rows+=feats(G[f'Demo pair {k} input'],G[f'Demo pair {k} output'])
import pandas as pd
df=pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(df.groupby(['nd1','nd2','d1','d2'])['label'].mean().to_string())

Now the pattern is clear: actual zone = expected_frame plus an extra column/row on one side... Zone height for demo1 A: 0..5 vs frame 0..4 → +1 row below. Demo1 B: 16..19 vs 16..18 → +1 below. Demo2 many: e.g. blk(0,17,2,2): zone rows0-2, frame -1..1 → +1 above (frame clipped at top). blk(3,10): zone 2..5, frame 2..4 → +1 below. So consistently zone = frame extended by exactly 1 in ONE direction per block — either below or above — and similarly columns extended by 1 on left or right.

Which direction? Look at demo1 A: extends down (rows 0..5+1=... wait zone rows 0..5, frame 0..4: extension below by 1. cols 5..10 vs frame 5..9: extension right by 1. So A: extend down AND right? But earlier I computed ring bbox rows0-6 cols4-11 (7x8) because I included... hmm my zone function now gave rows0-5, cols5-10, i.e., frame +1 down, +1 right. Earlier full-zone computation gave rows0-6 cols4-11 — that included... whatever, this new "adjacent cells" method found only cells orthogonally adjacent to perimeter. The zone (bbox of those cells) is rows0-5,cols5-10 = 6x6 frame around a 4x4 block plus 1 extra row/col each. For demo6: zone rows18-21, frame 18-20 → +1 below; cols3-6, frame 3-5 → +1 right. Consistent!

So rule candidate: ring = rectangle frame at distance 1 from block, with thickness 1, PLUS extend 1 extra cell beyond on one vertical side and one horizontal side. Which sides? Need a rule. In demo1 A, extra below and right. B: extra below, right. Demo2 blk(0,17): extra above & right. blk(3,10): extra below & right. Hmm not consistent.

Maybe extension depends on available space? Or maybe the extension is toward the nearest other block? Or maybe extension direction alternates? Let's look at pairs: demo2 blocks sorted. Extra rows: b0(0,17,-1→above), b1(3,10,below), b2(4,5,below)... both below mostly. Columns all right.

Demo3: zones vs frames: blk(0,6): zone rows0-2 frame -1..1 → +1 below; cols5-8 frame 5-7 → +1 right. blk(1,0): zone 0..3 frame 0..2 → +1 below; cols0-2 frame -1..1 → +1 right. Most are down/right. Except demo2 blk(0,17) which is +1 above. Why? Because extending down would overlap nothing... grid has 16 rows, block at rows0-1, h=2 → frame rows -1..1, ext below gives 0..2 fine. Extending above impossible (-1 row out of grid)! That explains it: extension goes to the side with more space? blk(0,17): above has less space (only 2 rows vs 16). So choose side with more room. Check others: demo8 blk(0,3): zone rows0-2, frame -1..1, so +1 below ✓. demo8 blk(2,0): zone 1..4, frame 1..3, +1 below ✓. col extensions: demo8 blk(3,7): cols6-15 frame 6-14, +1 right ✓. All cols right?? Check demo8 col extensions: blk(0,3): zone cols2-5, frame 2-4, +1 right. blk(2,0): zone 0-2, frame -1-1, +1 right. blk(6,1): zone 0-3, frame 0-2, +1 right. blk(9,1): same +1 right. blk(12,0): zone 0-2 frame -1-1 +1 right. All right.

Hmm but demo2 blk(0,17) extended above instead of below. Maybe rule: extend toward the farther side... demo2 blk(3,10): grid rows 0..27? block rows3-4. Below space bigger than above → extend below ✓. col: always extend right regardless. Wait demo2 all cols right, but some blocks have c0 near right edge (e.g. c0=25,w=2): blk(10,25): zone cols24-27, frame 24-26, +1 right would be out of grid (grid width?) mismatch count was low so ok.

Demo7 blk(1,7): zone cols6-9, frame 6-8, +1 right ✓. blk(8,2): cols1-8 frame1-7 +1 right ✓. Demo5: all right.

Row extension: demo2 blk(0,17) above. Others below. Rule maybe: extend away from the closer neighbor / into larger free area. For blk(0,17), extending below might conflict with something? Nothing below (rows2..27 empty). Hmm.

Alternative idea: maybe extension direction relates to the shadow! Shadow is drawn below the ring bottom. Maybe ring extends downward by 1 so that its shadow region gets wider? Actually maybe the ring includes one extra row to cover the shadow start... no, shadow starts at r0+h+1 = ring bottom+1.

Let me think differently: perhaps the ring is actually a rectangle scaled: ring dims = (h+2)x(w+2) where it's centered as much as possible, clipped. Demo1 A: h=4→6? got 7. No.

So all extensions are BELOW (and right)? Demo2 blk(0,17): ring rows0-2 = frame(-1,1) + row2 below ✓. Great, so universal: ring = frame(r0-1..r0+h, c0-1..c0+w) ∪ extra row r0+h+1 full width [c0-1..c0+w] and extra col c0+w+1 full height [r0-1..r0+h]. Wait but does the extra column exist for all? Recount demo1 A: zone rows0-6 cols4-11 from comps_of. Frame rows0-5 cols5-10. Extras: row 6, col 4, col 11. So extras on all four sides?! Rows 0-6 = extra above? no frame already covers 0-5.

Alternatively ring = dilation by 2 of block border? Block border (perimeter of block): dilate border by 2: for 4x4 block, border cells; dilation by 2 gives rectangle shrunk... perimeter dilated by k gives rect [r0-k, r0+h+k] x [c0-k, c0+w+k]. Demo1 A with k=2: rows -1..7, cols 4..11 — observed rows0-6. With k=1: rows0..6, cols5..11 — observed cols4-11. Mixed.

New idea: maybe ring height = h+2 and ring width = w+2, centered on block: rows r0-1..r0+h+1, cols c0-1..c0+w+1. Demo1 A: rows0-6, cols5-11. Observed cols4-11 (width 8). Off by one on left. What if the ring surrounds BOTH the block and its projected shadow up to the next shape? Eh.

What if ring extents = block bbox expanded by (h+1)//2? Demo1 A: expand by 2 each side: rows1-2→0-7? no.

Time to consider: maybe ring = block dilated by ceil(h/2)? Demo1 A h=4: dilate 2: rows -1..8, cols 4..12. No.

Honestly, maybe I should reconsider the problem entirely. Perhaps these outputs show: for each block, draw a "frame" (rectangle outline) around the block at radius 1, AND fill below with shadow; the observed ring A being 7x8 might be frame of rows0-5 cols4-11 minus... no, it's filled outline? Rows0-6 cols4-11: is it just border of 7x8 rect? Row0 all 3, rows1-4 only cols4,5,10,11, row5-6 all 3. Yes it's the border of a 7x8 rectangle! So ring = border of rect 7x8. Block 4x4 inside at offset (1,2) from rect top-left... rect center rows1.5? block center rows 2.5. Rect center rows 2.5 too (0..6 → 3). cols rect 4..11 center 7.5, block center 7.5. So ring rect is centered on block, size (2*floor?) rows: h=4, rect h=7? Odd.

Border of rect R around block B such that... maybe rect size = block + 2*(block dim // something)... Demo6: block 2x2, rect 4x4 → double. Demo1 A: block 4x4, rect 7x8?? not double. Unless I mislabeled: maybe there are actually two rectangles: 6x6 border (rows0-5,cols5-10) and something else adding row6 and cols4,11? Or maybe the output draws border of rect = dilate(block bbox, by 1) ∪ ... 

Actually check demo8 big block (8x8 at rows3-10 cols7-14): ring rows2-11 cols6-15 = 10x9 border. Double would be 16x16. Frame r0-1..r0+h+1, c0-1..c0+w+1 → 10x9 ✓ matches! And cols6-15 ✓. So why demo1 A has extra row/col? Distance consideration: maybe ring must NOT touch... no. What if the ring must have even dimensions? Demo6 ring 4x4 even ✓. Demo1 A 7x8 odd/even. def bb(gi):
    H,W=len(gi),len(gi[0]); bl=[]; seen=set()
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            v=gi[r][c]
            if v==0: continue
            if (r,c) in seen: continue
            col=v
            stack=[(r,c)]; cells=set()
            while stack:
                x,y=stack.pop()
                if (x,y) in cells or not(0<=x<H and 0<=y<W) or gi[x][y]!=v: continue
                cells.add((x,y)); seen.add((x,y))
                for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)): stack.append((x+dr,y+dc))
            rs=[x for x,_ in cells]; cs=[y for _,y in cells]
            bl.append((min(rs),min(cs),max(rs)-min(rs)+1,max(cs)-min(cs)+1,col))
    return bl
# check demo1 blocks: print each with ring zone found earlier plus expected
